about: Delivery directions for chapter 2's voices (eleven_v4 audio tags). 'default' is per speaker; 'say' is a line's full spoken text with tags, which must equal the page text once the tags are removed. tools/directions.py checks that and writes voices.json.

say.p1-open: [wry] St Aldhelm's, a Tuesday in October, twenty past seven. [short pause] Three months after the Marrow Show, the interim vicar has talked you into learning to ring the bells.
say.p1a-2: [dry] There is no bicycle in the rack by the lychgate. Hugh Daventry rings the treble, writes the parish magazine and sets the quiz at the Plough. [short pause] Hugh is never late.
say.p1b-1: [pleased, precise] Sergeant Adeyemi. I had you at forty per cent to turn up.
say.p1b-3: [satisfied] A hundred. [short pause] It's very satisfying.
say.p1c-1: [much too loud] Win Haskett. Tower captain. You'll be the policeman.
say.p1c-3: [loud, stern] Watch the ropes, not the people. [short pause] And don't touch anything with a rope on it.
say.p1d-3: [loud, brisk] Ten rows and you're home. The treble leads, the rest follow. [drily] Hugh has the treble, if he turns up.
say.p2a-1: [quiet] Margaret Pike pours tea from a flask on the windowsill. She puts out two cups, looks at the second one, [short pause] and puts it back in the basket.
say.p2b-3: [loud, warning] Don't write it on the board. Hugh hates anyone writing on his board.
say.p2c-1: [loud, ringing call] Look to. Treble's going. [short pause] She's gone.
say.p2d-1: [low] At a quarter past eight, the lights go out.
say.p2d-2: [tense, quiet] The ringing goes on in the dark, and goes wrong. A bell is missing from the pattern, or two are. You cannot tell. [short pause] Somewhere below you, something falls.
say.p2d-4: [breezy, a little out of breath] Fuse box. It's older than the bells.
say.p3-open: [quiet, grave] Hugh Daventry is at the foot of the tower stair, where it comes down into the vestry. Dr Achebe is kneeling beside him. [short pause] She looks up and shakes her head.
say.p3a-4: [quiet, wry] I came down to put the kettle on. I found him. [short pause] Statistically, that makes me interesting.
say.p3c-2: [weary] I was in the bath, Sam. [short pause] Tell me it's an accident.
say.p3c-4: [sharp] Then why did you ring me and not just an ambulance?
say.p4e-2: [loud, pointed] I don't look at my phone in the tower. [short pause] Some do.
say.p5b-1: [smooth, sorrowful] Sergeant. Inspector. Terrible business. Hugh was a friend. [short pause] Well. Hugh was a historian, which is nearly the same thing.
say.p5c-1: [smooth, confident] On the five, ringing, every blow, start to finish. Five is my bell. Ask anyone in the band.
say.p5e-3: [smooth, quickly] A commission. Another church. [short pause] I'm not at liberty.
say.p6b-1: [into a microphone, cheerful] Round two. Question seven. [short pause] In what year did Monotype release the typeface Gill Sans?
say.p6b-3: [quiet, thoughtful] He was going to ask the whole village. Then tell them the answer in print.
say.p7b-1: [bright, salesman] Sergeant! Come to buy a schoolhouse? Four bedrooms, original features, a bell nobody's allowed to ring.
say.p7d-4: [deflated] That's not going in the brochure, is it.
say.p8b-2: [fond, dry] My father had a railway timetable in those letters. He kept it in the downstairs toilet.
say.p8b-5: [calm, precise] I'd put Victorian at four per cent.
say.p8c-1: [calm, amused] On base rates, Inspector, it is usually the person who found him. That's me. [short pause] I'd put myself at eleven per cent.
say.p8c-3: [calm] I don't do my parishioners out loud. [short pause] I do them at night.
say.p8e-3: [mild] It was here this morning. I assumed it was a ringer.
say.p9d-4: [quick, pleased] Take the four out. 4 2 5 1 3 becomes 2 5 1 3, and by note that's 2 4 1 3. Then 4 2 3 1. Then 4 3 2 1. [short pause] Every row.
say.p10h-1: [breaking, bitter] He was going to print it. In the magazine. Nine thousand pounds, and a correction, in the magazine.
say.p10h-2: [quiet, hollow] I only wanted the page back. He wouldn't let go of it. [short pause] Hugh never let go of anything.
say.p10h-3: [cold, quiet] Neither do I, Mr Cole.
say.p10i-4: [hushed] When they stand, the tenor, which nobody has rung all week, speaks once on its own.
say.p10i-5: [very quiet] Up on its wheel, something small and yellow looks down the tower at you.
